$comment: One ELEMENT of a vector register in an aarch64 inline-asm template — `umov %0, %1.d[1]`, `mov %0, %1.d[0]`, `mov %w0, %1.s[3]`, `ins %0.d[0], %1` with its `mov` alias, and `ins %0.b[0], %w1` on a `"+w"` operand whose other fifteen bytes must survive (D-ASM-DIALECT-GAPS-A-REFERENCE-ASSEMBLER-ACCEPTS). The P68 round-7 base refused the template at its grammar. ✔MEASURED 2026-09-21: aarch64-linux-gnu-gcc 13.3.0 and clang 18.1.3 run it to 42 at -O0 and -O2 under qemu-aarch64. ⚠ ELF aarch64 only, by construction: the example reads the halves of an IEEE binary128 `long double`, which Linux gives aarch64 and Apple's arm64 ABI does not (its `long double` is binary64). ★ The `release` arm: every value reaches its template through an operand and every result leaves through one, so the optimized pipeline cannot fold a check away.
